description: Nine ways of changing a signal's sign, in 4HP, each with its own input and output and each input reading the one above it when empty

inputs.text: The signal for that row; an empty jack reads the nearest patched input above it, so one signal into the top jack feeds all nine rows

outputs.text: Carries the input with every negative voltage replaced by 0V
Carries the input with every positive voltage replaced by 0V
Carries the input with negative voltages made positive
Carries the input flipped within the inversion range on the menu, so at the default 0V to 10V an input of 3V comes out as 7V
Carries the input with 5V added, which moves a -5V to 5V signal up to 0V to 10V
Carries the input with 5V taken away, which moves a 0V to 10V signal down to -5V to 5V
Carries 10V while the input is 1V or more, and 0V below that
Carries 10V while the input is below 1V, and 0V at 1V or more

notes: the nine rows are independent transformations of whatever reaches their own input; nothing is chained from one output to the next
menu: Inversion-range — sets the range the !Rng output flips a value within, 0V to 10V unless you change it
Quantize mode — rounds the output to the nearest step of the size chosen, from a twelfth of a volt up to 5V, and is Off unless you set it
Clipping range — clamps every output to the range chosen, -12V to 12V unless you change it, and Off lets the output run to any voltage
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed
Gate-high detect-level — sets the voltage at which an incoming gate counts as high, 1V or more unless you change it
Gate-high output-level — sets the voltage a gate output carries while high, 10V unless you change it
Gate-low output-level — sets the voltage a gate output carries while low, 0V unless you change it
